heading: THE KENSHO REVOLUTION: Inside the AI-Driven 'eMAXIS Neo' Series Upending the Japanese Mutual Fund Market
story:
By The VILFIN TV Financial Desk | Exclusive Report

* Note: This fund is for Japanese market only.

The traditional index fund is facing an existential crisis. For decades, passive investing meant simply tracking companies based on their market capitalization—buying the biggest companies and ignoring the underlying narrative. But as we navigate 2026, Mitsubishi UFJ Asset Management’s eMAXIS Neo series has officially proven that passive investing no longer needs to be "dumb."

Powered by S&P Kensho's Natural Language Processing (NLP) AI, the eMAXIS Neo series has stripped the steering wheel from human stock-pickers and legacy algorithms. Kensho’s AI acts as a tireless, omniscient analyst, reading millions of pages of regulatory filings, annual reports, and earnings transcripts. If an old-school legacy manufacturer suddenly dedicates a massive portion of its R&D to robotics or clean energy, the AI detects the shift in the text and instantly flags the stock for inclusion during its semi-annual rebalance.

The result? A suite of 14 highly concentrated, hyper-growth thematic funds that have delivered some of the most astronomical—and volatile—returns in the Japanese retail market. In this VILFIN TV Exclusive, we break down the performance, the underlying stock engines, and the future outlook for every single fund in the eMAXIS Neo ecosystem.

The Space & Skies Frontier: Leaving Earth Behind

The commercialization of orbit is no longer a billionaire’s vanity project; it is the backbone of modern global telecommunications and defense.

eMAXIS Neo Space Development (宇宙開発)

Trading near ¥62,600, this fund is the undisputed superstar of the Neo lineup, boasting a staggering +170.9% 1-year return leading into mid-2026. The fund captures the explosion of private aerospace contracts and satellite deployments. Rather than relying on legacy airlines, the Kensho index heavily weights new-space innovators and defense contractors. Major holdings driving this growth include Rocket Lab USA (a pioneer in dedicated small satellite launch), L3Harris Technologies, and legacy aerospace titan Lockheed Martin.

Future Outlook: As low-earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations become the standard for global broadband and military surveillance, this fund will remain highly tethered to U.S. defense budgets and launch-cost reductions.

eMAXIS Neo Drones (ドローン)

While Space looks up, Drones look strictly at the lower atmosphere. Delivering a massive +96.2% 1-year return, this fund (trading around ¥47,500) has capitalized on the convergence of commercial logistics and modern warfare. Companies manufacturing autonomous aerial vehicles and the sensory software required to pilot them have seen aggressive re-ratings, anchored by companies heavily investing in uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) software and precision hardware.

Future Outlook: The drone market is transitioning from hardware to software. The future winners in this index won't necessarily be the companies building the plastic rotors, but the firms coding the swarm-intelligence algorithms that allow thousands of drones to operate in synchronized airspace.

The Core Tech Backbone: The Invisible Infrastructure

You cannot build the future of the global economy without the software and routing infrastructure to support it.

eMAXIS Neo AI Technology (AIテクノロジー)

Currently hovering around ¥27,900, the AI fund has logged a phenomenal +122.1% 1-year return. This fund does not just track the companies using AI; it tracks the companies building it. By heavily weighting semiconductor giants, data-center infrastructure companies, and machine-learning algorithm developers, it acts as the "picks and shovels" play for the AI gold rush. The index is powered by foundational hardware and software giants like NVIDIA, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and cloud infrastructure leader Microsoft.

Future Outlook: The initial hype cycle has passed, and we are now entering the enterprise execution phase. The AI index will likely see a culling, dropping consumer AI novelties in favor of B2B heavyweights dominating corporate cloud environments.

eMAXIS Neo Communication DX (コミュニケーションDX)

Often overshadowed by its AI counterpart, Communication Digital Transformation (DX) is the silent enabler, turning in a steady +41.5% 1-year return. This fund captures the enterprise shift toward unified communications, cloud routing, and decentralized team platforms, heavily leaning on companies like Zoom Video Communications, Cisco Systems, and Twilio.

Future Outlook: As "work from anywhere" evolves into highly secure, persistent remote environments, the telecom software and cyber-secured routing companies in this index will provide the stable, recurring revenue often missing from pure-play AI startups.

The Energy Transition: The Subsidized Boom

The global energy transition is being fueled by trillions of dollars in government subsidies, making these sectors highly resilient to consumer market fluctuations.

eMAXIS Neo Clean Tech (クリーンテック)

Trading around ¥17,700, this fund captures the broader renewable infrastructure boom, posting a massive +186.0% 1-year return. Driven by heavyweight holdings in companies like SolarEdge Technologies, utility tracker Nextracker Inc., and solar-panel manufacturer JinkoSolar, it targets the hardware necessary for solar, wind, and geothermal generation. While it has seen slight short-term pullbacks in the past, its current long-term growth profile remains heavily subsidized by the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act (IRA).

Future Outlook: The narrative is shifting from "power generation" to "power storage." The Kensho AI is actively re-weighting this index toward utility-scale battery manufacturers and smart-grid infrastructure companies.

eMAXIS Neo Hydrogen Economy (水素エコノミー)

Sitting near ¥26,200, the Hydrogen Economy fund has been the ultimate hidden gem, delivering an astonishing +189.0% 1-year return. Tracking heavyweights like Bloom Energy, Ballard Power Systems, and cryogenic equipment maker Chart Industries, this fund is betting on hydrogen fuel cells for commercial shipping, aviation, and factory power grids—places where traditional batteries are simply too heavy.

Future Outlook: Highly volatile but fundamentally vital. As European and Asian nations mandate zero-emission commercial transport, hydrogen is the only mathematically viable solution for heavy freight.

The Physical Automation Wave: Battling the Labor Crisis

With populations aging across the developed world, physical automation is no longer a luxury for corporations; it is a matter of survival.

eMAXIS Neo Robotics (ロボット)

Priced around ¥27,200, this fund has delivered a rock-solid +54.3% 1-year return. Unlike software AI, robotics requires massive physical capital expenditure. The fund tracks global leaders in factory automation, surgical robotics, and warehouse logistics, including legacy Japanese industrial powerhouses like Fanuc, alongside U.S. software-automation leaders like UiPath and iRobot.

Future Outlook: The Kensho index will increasingly blur the lines between AI and Robotics. The next massive leap in this fund's NAV will come from "embodied AI"—robots that don't just follow programmed tracks, but use onboard spatial computing to navigate unpredictable environments.

eMAXIS Neo Autonomous Driving (自動運転)

Separating the intelligence of the vehicle from the chassis, this fund clocked a stellar +73.0% 1-year return. Instead of just buying automakers, the index targets LiDAR manufacturers, sensor developers, and neural-network trainers. Top components include semiconductor designers like STMicroelectronics and Allegro MicroSystems, alongside next-generation EV software players like China's XPeng.

Future Outlook: The real value in autonomous driving is in the software licensing, not the metal. Look for this index to heavily favor tech companies over legacy car manufacturers in the coming rebalance cycles.

Next-Generation Mobility & Reality

The way humans move—and the worlds they inhabit—are undergoing a radical digital transformation.

eMAXIS Neo Electric Vehicles (電気自動車)

This sector has faced severe macroeconomic headwinds recently, battling global tariff wars, supply chain crunches, and margin compression, resulting in a more muted +15.2% 1-year return. However, the Kensho index methodology ensures it doesn't just hold legacy auto stocks like Tesla and Rivian; it captures battery chemistry innovators, lithium refiners like Albemarle, and charging network developers.

Future Outlook: The EV war is moving from the showroom floor to the supply chain. The index will likely pivot toward advanced solid-state battery manufacturers and raw material processing.

eMAXIS Neo Virtual Reality (バーチャルリアリティ)

Despite cyclical "Metaverse" hype, this fund has delivered an explosive +88.5% 1-year return, pushing its NAV past the ¥18,000 mark. Driven by hardware innovators like Kopin Corp, spatial software developers like Unity Software, and big-tech ecosystem players like Meta Platforms, it captures the push toward enterprise simulation and immersive digital environments.

Future Outlook: VR is quietly becoming essential B2B infrastructure. As military training, medical surgery simulators, and industrial design move entirely into spatial computing, this fund will shed its "gaming" reputation.

Deep Science: Rewriting the Human Code

The longest-term "moonshots" in the eMAXIS Neo lineup rely on fundamental scientific breakthroughs rather than software iterations.

eMAXIS Neo Genetic Engineering (遺伝子工学)

Boasting a +38.4% 1-year return, this is arguably the most volatile fund in the entire series. Driven by CRISPR technology and mRNA advancements, its underlying biotech stocks—such as CRISPR Therapeutics, Moderna, and genomic-sequencing giant Illumina—can surge 200% on a successful FDA clinical trial or collapse overnight on a failure.

Future Outlook: The era of personalized medicine is here. As gene editing moves from clinical trials to commercial treatments for rare diseases, this index offers immense, albeit high-risk, upside.

eMAXIS Neo Wearables (ウェアラブル)

Delivering a steady +44.7% 1-year return, this sector has stealthily transitioned from consumer pedometers to FDA-approved medical diagnostic equipment. The companies in this index, such as Dexcom (continuous glucose monitors) and Apple (via its health tracking), are developing cardiac arrhythmia detectors and neurological sensors.

Future Outlook: As global healthcare systems shift to preventative remote monitoring to save costs, wearable tech will become integrated directly into health insurance and hospital networks.

eMAXIS Neo Nanotechnology (ナノテクノロジー)

The science of the infinitesimally small has quietly returned +61.2% over the past year. This fund tracks companies working on advanced semiconductor materials, quantum computing hardware, and next-generation carbon nanotubes for energy storage, anchored by material science heavyweights like Applied Materials and Thermo Fisher Scientific.

Future Outlook: Nanotech is the bottleneck for the entire tech sector. You cannot build faster AI or better batteries without atomic-level material science, making this fund a deep-value play on the future of hardware.

The Financial Revolution

eMAXIS Neo Fintech (フィンテック)

Money never sleeps, but how it moves is changing daily. Delivering a solid +51.8% 1-year return, the Fintech fund captures the disruption of legacy banking, tracking everything from digital payment gateways and blockchain infrastructure platforms to algorithmic lending software. Core holdings include crypto-exchange operator Coinbase, digital payment leader Block (formerly Square), and PayPal.

Future Outlook: High interest rates have forced a consolidation in the Fintech sector, killing off weak startups and leaving a highly concentrated index of massively profitable payment processors. As cross-border transactions become instantaneous, these survivors are positioned for global institutional scaling.

The VILFIN TV Verdict: Strategy and The Currency Elephant

For Japanese retail investors utilizing their NISA Growth Investment Quota (成長投資枠), the eMAXIS Neo series offers unparalleled, institutional-grade access to global innovation. The Kensho AI's ability to read and react to corporate pivots ensures these funds never become bogged down by stagnant legacy companies.

However, VILFIN TV analysts must issue a critical warning: Currency Risk.

Every single fund in the eMAXIS Neo series is completely unhedged, and the underlying assets are overwhelmingly U.S.-listed equities. The massive 100%+ returns seen in funds like Space Development, AI Technology, and Hydrogen over the past year were heavily amplified by the historical weakness of the Japanese Yen against the U.S. Dollar.

If you are buying into the Neo series today, you are making two bets: one on the technological theme, and one on the exchange rate. If the Bank of Japan normalizes rates and the Yen aggressively strengthens, the JPY-denominated value of these funds will face a severe headwind—even if the underlying U.S. tech stocks are hitting all-time highs.

The Strategy: Do not chase yesterday's returns. Build a "Neo Barbell." Pair a high-growth software theme (like AI or VR) with a physical, heavily subsidized industrial theme (like Robotics or Clean Tech). By letting Kensho’s AI pick the winners inside those sectors, you can capture the explosive upside of the 21st century without anchoring your entire portfolio to a single narrative.

Disclaimer: This VILFIN TV Exclusive is for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial advice. Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks; read all scheme-related documents carefully before investing.

For more details - https://emaxis.am.mufg.jp/lp/neo/

heading: ഡിജിറ്റൽ യുഗത്തിലെ 'പേപ്പർ വാലുകൾ': എൻ.ആർ.ഐ നികുതിയിളവുകൾ ഇനിയും എന്ന് ഓട്ടോമേറ്റഡ് ആകും?
story:
VilfinTV Exclusive Report | By VilfinTV News Desk

ഒരു വിരൽത്തുമ്പിൽ ബാങ്ക് അക്കൗണ്ടുകൾ തുറക്കാനും സെക്കൻഡുകൾക്കുള്ളിൽ അന്താരാഷ്ട്ര ഓഹരി വ്യാപാരം നടത്താനും സാധിക്കുന്ന ഡിജിറ്റൽ ഇന്ത്യയിലാണ് നാം ജീവിക്കുന്നത്. എന്നാൽ, എൻ.ആർ.ഐ (Non-Resident Indian) നികുതിയിളവുകളുടെ കാര്യത്തിലേക്ക് വരുമ്പോൾ രാജ്യം ഇന്നും വളരെ പഴക്കമുള്ള 'മാനുവൽ' സമീപനമാണ് തുടരുന്നതെന്ന ആക്ഷേപം ശക്തമാണ്.

തങ്ങളുടെ കഠിനാധ്വാനത്തിലൂടെ നേടുന്ന ഇന്ത്യൻ വരുമാനത്തിന്മേൽ 31.2% എന്ന ഉയർന്ന NRO TDS ബാധ്യത ഒഴിവാക്കാൻ പ്രവാസികൾ ഓരോ വർഷവും കടന്നുപോകേണ്ടി വരുന്നത് അനാവശ്യവും സങ്കീർണ്ണവുമായ ഒരു ബ്യൂറോക്രാറ്റിക് കടമ്പയിലൂടെയാണ്.

എന്താണ് ഈ പ്രവാസി നികുതി ദുരിതം?

ആദായനികുതി പോർട്ടലിൽ ലോഗിൻ ചെയ്ത്, വിദേശത്തെ ടാക്സ് റെസിഡൻസി സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റ് (TRC) അപ്ലോഡ് ചെയ്ത്, ഓൺലൈനായി പുതിയ ഫോം സബ്മിറ്റ് ചെയ്താലും പ്രവാസിയുടെ ജോലി തീരുന്നില്ല. അവിടെ നിന്നും ഡൗൺലോഡ് ചെയ്യുന്ന പി.ഡി.എഫ് (PDF) ഫയലുകൾ ഓരോ ബാങ്കിലും ബ്രോക്കറേജ് സ്ഥാപനങ്ങളിലും പ്രവാസികൾ വീണ്ടും നേരിട്ട് ഇമെയിൽ വഴി അയച്ചു കൊടുക്കേണ്ടി വരുന്നു.

രാജ്യത്തിന്റെ ഡിജിറ്റൽ ഇൻഫ്രാസ്ട്രക്ചർ ഇത്രയധികം മുന്നേറിയിട്ടും, എന്തുകൊണ്ട് ബാങ്കുകൾക്ക് നേരിട്ട് ആദായനികുതി പോർട്ടലിൽ നിന്ന് ഈ വിവരങ്ങൾ പരിശോധിക്കാൻ (Fetch) സാധിക്കുന്നില്ല?

എന്തുകൊണ്ട് ഇൻകം ടാക്സ് വകുപ്പ് ഓട്ടോമേഷൻ ഇൻഫ്രാസ്ട്രക്ചർ നിർമ്മക്ുന്നില്ല?

സാങ്കേതികമായി വളരെ എളുപ്പത്തിൽ ഒരു API വഴി പരിഹരിക്കാവുന്ന ഒരു പ്രശ്നമായിട്ടും, ഇതിനായുള്ള ഒരു കേന്ദ്രീകൃത സംവിധാനം (Centralized Automated Infrastructure) സർക്കാർ നിർമ്മിക്കാത്തതിന് പിന്നിൽ മൂന്ന് പ്രധാന കാരണങ്ങളാണുള്ളത്:

ബാങ്കുകളുടെ മേലുള്ള നിയമപരമായ ബാധ്യത (Section 195):

ഇന്ത്യൻ ആദായനികുതി നിയമത്തിലെ സെക്ഷൻ 195 പ്രകാരം, കുറഞ്ഞ നിരക്കിൽ നികുതി ഈടാക്കണമെങ്കിൽ അതിന്റെ പൂർണ്ണമായ രേഖകൾ കൈവശം സൂക്ഷിക്കേണ്ട ഉത്തരവാദിത്തം ബാങ്കുകൾക്കാണ്. ഭാവിയിൽ ഒരു ഓഡിറ്റിംഗ് ഉണ്ടായാൽ, വെറുമൊരു 'ഡിജിറ്റൽ സിഗ്നൽ' കാണിച്ചാൽ ടാക്സ് ഓഫീസർമാർ അംഗീകരിക്കില്ല. നിയമം വഴി മാറ്റങ്ങൾ വരുത്താതെ, ആദായനികുതി വകുപ്പ് നൽകുന്ന ഒരു API ലിങ്ക് മാത്രം വിശ്വസിച്ച് റിസ്ക് എടുക്കാൻ ബാങ്കുകൾ തയ്യാറാകില്ല.

പരസ്പരം ബന്ധമില്ലാത്ത വിവരശേഖരങ്ങൾ (Siloed Databases):

ആദായനികുതി വകുപ്പിന്റെ വ്യവസ്ഥകൾ ഇന്നും പല തട്ടുകളിലാണ്. സാധാരണ നികുതിദായകർ ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്ന 'ഇ-ഫയലിംഗ് പോർട്ടലും', ബാങ്കുകൾ നികുതി വിവരങ്ങൾ റിപ്പോർട്ട് ചെയ്യാൻ ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്ന 'TRACES പോർട്ടലും' രണ്ട് വ്യത്യസ്ത സെർവറുകളിലാണ് പ്രവർത്തിക്കുന്നത്. ഈ രണ്ട് ഭീമൻ ഡാറ്റാബേസുകളെയും സ്വകാര്യ ബാങ്കുകളുമായി തത്സമയം (Real-time) സുരക്ഷിതമായി ബന്ധിപ്പിക്കാൻ ആവശ്യമായ സാങ്കേതിക ഏകോപനവും സുരക്ഷാ മാനദണ്ഡങ്ങളും നടപ്പിലാക്കാൻ നികുതി വകുപ്പ് ഇതുവരെ തയ്യാറായിട്ടില്ല.

സർക്കാരിന്റെ സാമ്പത്തിക താല്പര്യങ്ങൾ (Interest-Free Loans):

ഏറ്റവും പ്രായോഗികമായ മറ്റൊരു കാരണം, ഈ സങ്കീർണ്ണതകൾ വഴി സർക്കാരിന് ലഭിക്കുന്ന താല്ക്കാലിക സാമ്പത്തിക ലാഭമാണ്. പേപ്പർവർക്കുകൾ പൂർത്തിയാക്കാൻ സാധിക്കാത്ത പ്രവാസികളിൽ നിന്നും ബാങ്കുകൾ ഉയർന്ന നിരക്കിൽ (31.2%) നികുതി ഈടാക്കി സർക്കാരിലേക്ക് അടയ്ക്കുന്നു. ഒരു വർഷത്തിന് ശേഷം പ്രവാസികൾ റിട്ടേൺ (ITR) ഫയൽ ചെയ്ത് ഈ തുക തിരികെ വാങ്ങുമെങ്കിലും, അതുവരെയുള്ള 12 മുതൽ 18 മാസങ്ങളിൽ കോടിക്കണക്കിന് രൂപയാണ് സർക്കാരിന് യാതൊരു പലിശയുമില്ലാതെ (Interest-free loan) പ്രവാസികളിൽ നിന്നും ലഭിക്കുന്നത്. അതിനാൽ തന്നെ ഈ സംവിധാനം എളുപ്പമാക്കാൻ സർക്കാരിന് വലിയ സാമ്പത്തിക അടിയന്തിരതയില്ല.

പ്രവാസികൾ എന്ത് ചെയ്യണം?

ഒരു സാമ്പത്തിക വർഷം ആരംഭിക്കുമ്പോൾ തന്നെ വിദേശത്തെ നിങ്ങളുടെ ടാക്സ് റെസിഡൻസി രേഖകൾ കൃത്യമായി ശേഖരിക്കുകയും, ഓൺലൈൻ ഫോമുകൾ മുൻകൂട്ടി സമർപ്പിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുക എന്നത് മാത്രമാണ് നിലവിലെ ഏക പോംവഴി. സിസ്റ്റം പൂർണ്ണമായും ഓട്ടോമേറ്റഡ് ആകുന്നത് വരെ, കൃത്യമായ പേപ്പർവർക്കുകൾ മാത്രമാണ് നിങ്ങളുടെ നിക്ഷേപങ്ങളെ ഉയർന്ന നികുതികളിൽ നിന്നും സംരക്ഷിക്കുന്നതിനുള്ള ഏക ആയുധം.

കൂടുതൽ സാമ്പത്തിക വാർത്തകൾക്കും മാർക്കറ്റ് അപ്ഡേറ്റുകൾക്കുമായി VilfinTV സന്ദർശിക്കുക.

heading: Paper Trails in the Digital Age: When Will NRI Tax Deductions Finally Be Automated?
story:
VilfinTV Exclusive Report | By VilfinTV News Desk

We live in a digital India where bank accounts can be opened with a tap and international stock trading can be executed in seconds. However, when it comes to Non-Resident Indian (NRI) tax deductions, there is strong criticism that the country continues to rely on a highly outdated, 'manual' approach.

To avoid the high 31.2% NRO TDS burden on the Indian income they earn through hard work, NRIs must navigate an unnecessary and complex bureaucratic hurdle every single year.

What is this NRI Tax Misery?

Even after logging into the Income Tax portal, uploading a foreign Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), and submitting the new form online, the NRI's job is not done. They must then download PDF files and manually email them directly to every single bank and brokerage institution.

With the country's digital infrastructure advancing so rapidly, why can't banks directly fetch this information from the Income Tax portal?

Why Isn't the Income Tax Department Building Automation Infrastructure?

Despite this being a problem that could easily be solved technically via an API, there are three primary reasons why the government has not built a Centralized Automated Infrastructure for this:

Legal Liability on Banks (Section 195):

Under Section 195 of the Indian Income Tax Act, the responsibility to retain complete documentation for applying a lower tax rate falls entirely on the banks. If there is an audit in the future, tax officers will not accept a mere 'digital signal.' Without legislative changes, banks are unwilling to take the risk of trusting just an API link provided by the Income Tax Department.

Siloed Databases:

The systems of the Income Tax Department remain heavily fragmented. The 'e-Filing portal' used by regular taxpayers and the 'TRACES portal' used by banks to report tax data operate on entirely different servers. The tax department has not yet been willing to implement the technical coordination and security standards required to safely connect these two massive databases with private banks in real-time.

Financial Interests of the Government (Interest-Free Loans):

Another highly practical reason is the temporary financial gain the government receives from these complexities. When NRIs are unable to complete the paperwork, banks deduct tax at the maximum rate (31.2%) and remit it to the government. Even though NRIs can claim a refund after filing their returns (ITR) a year later, during those 12 to 18 months, the government essentially receives billions of rupees as an interest-free loan from NRIs. Therefore, the government has no major financial urgency to simplify this system.

What Should NRIs Do?

The only current solution is to accurately collect your foreign tax residency documents at the very beginning of the financial year and submit the online forms well in advance. Until the system becomes fully automated, meticulous paperwork remains your only weapon to protect your investments from high taxes.
